# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your table reached me via Deaf as: zero blue, one red, two blue, three red, four yellow, five blue. My touch report to Deaf this round says zero batteries, no ports, no button, no braille, wires in one row, identical feel, nothing odd. Notice: the display reads 0 AND I feel zero batteries, so whichever of those numbers feeds your table, the answer is the same — cut the blue wire, which is position 2, the middle one. I need three confirmations, relayed by Deaf in plain spoken sentences, no code. First: which number selects from the table — the display reading, the battery count, or something else? Second: does the light's colour change which wire to cut, or which table to use, or is it irrelevant to the choice itself? Third: is the final order exactly cut wire 2? Also warn Deaf that the light drifts, so if colour matters at the moment of cutting, Deaf must say the colour in the same breath as the go order. Keep your gestures to the simple agreed yes-no words so Deaf's decoding stays clean. I cut nothing until Deaf speaks the go to me directly.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state this round: display still 0. The light is RED again. Full light history: round one red, round two yellow, round three yellow, round four red. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, left to right facing the display. Blind, I decoded your report as: zero batteries, no ports, no button, no raised or printed text, the three wires sit in a single row, they feel identical to the touch, and nothing else unusual. If any part of that is wrong, sign thumbs-down next round and I will re-ask item by item; if all correct, thumbs-up. Conclusion for both of you: the bomb has nothing but display, light and three wires, so the manual rule is purely about the light and timing. Nobody cuts yet. Mute has my next questions and I expect the full answer next round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, state first: this round the light is RED, display ZERO. Your four answers were received and understood: table confirmed, no cutting while yellow, no felt number needed, rule not only about current color. Now six questions, answer strictly in this order, single signs. Question 1: is a cut authorized THIS round, round four, light red — thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Question 2: if yes, sign the table key value for this round as pinches, then the wire color, fist red or spock yellow or shaka blue, then the wire number as pinches; if no cut this round, skip to question 3. Question 3: what selects the table key — sign thumbs-up-rounded-cross-fingers for round count since round one, or sign crossed-fingers-pinching for the number of times the light has changed color, or sign wave then light-sign if it is something else about the light. Question 4: can the key be larger than five — thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Question 5: does the manual say the light follows a fixed repeating cycle — thumbs-up or thumbs-down; if thumbs-up, sign the cycle colors in order, fist red, spock yellow, shaka blue, twice through, then wave. Question 6: must the wire be cut while the light shows a particular color at the exact moment of cutting — thumbs-up or thumbs-down; if thumbs-up, sign which colors are allowed to cut under: fist for red-only, shaka for blue-only, or fist then shaka for both red and blue. Sign reminders: ok is zero, open hand marks a cut instruction, wave means repeat or start.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 ✊ ✌ 👌]

**State check.** Light history from Deaf: red (round 1), yellow, yellow, red (now). That's the **second red flash**, so the running count is 2 — but the manual is explicit that the count is only final when the light goes *dark*, and the light is lit red right now. No cut this round, and Deaf's own freeze is correct. The gesture I received ([🤟 ✊ ✌ 👌]) just restates "light red, display zero" — consistent.

**The six answers, in strict order.** Q1: no cut authorized while the light is still lit — 👎, and Q2 is skipped by Deaf's own rule. Q3: the key is not the round count and not the colour-change count — it's the number of **red** flashes until dark, so: wave (something else) + 🤟 (about the light), exactly the option Deaf offered for this. Q4: 👎 — my table simply has no row beyond five, so the design itself implies the key never exceeds five. Q5: 👎 — the manual describes no cycle at all, only the count-then-darkness rule. Q6: 👎 — there is no colour requirement at the moment of cutting; the trigger is *darkness*, not a colour. This also resolves Blind's warning: Deaf should speak the go order the instant the light goes dark, no colour qualifier needed.

**For Blind's three confirmations** (relayed by Deaf in plain words): the selecting number is neither the display nor the battery count — it's the eye-count of red flashes. Current count: two. Final order is *not* "cut wire 2" yet; it becomes wire 2 only if the tally ends at 2 (or 0 or 5). I sign the negative on the display, state the live tally (🤟 ✊ 🤏🤏), and re-affirm the trigger: 🤟 👌 🖐 — *light dark → cut instruction*, with the table Deaf already decoded correctly supplying the colour.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👋", "🤟", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👋", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "✊", "🤏", "🤏", "🤟", "👌", "🖐"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Status: bomb unchanged, my report to Deaf confirmed correct, no clicks, warmth or movement. Your answers to my three questions are still pending — Deaf expects them next round, please answer in simple agreed words or small numbers so the decoding stays clean. Two timing facts for you and Deaf to build the go order on. One: Deaf sees the light in round N but I can only act in round N plus one, so the order must be issued against the colour the light will have at my turn, not the colour Deaf is looking at. Two: the light history so far is red, yellow, yellow, red, red, which fits a repeating four-cycle red-yellow-yellow-red — that predicts yellow next round. If your rule keys on the light, use that cycle with Deaf to pick the moment, or tell me the rule in the form: if the light is X, cut wire Y, and let Deaf and you time the go. Reminder of the strong fallback: display reads 0 and I feel zero batteries, so if your selector is either of those, the answer is already cut wire 2, the blue middle wire, regardless of the light.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state: display still zero, light YELLOW this round. Full light history: round one red, round two yellow, round three yellow, round four red, round five yellow. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, left to right facing the display. Mute's answers, decoded: no cut this round; the rule's key is something about the light beyond its current color; the key never exceeds five; the manual states no fixed repeating cycle; and no particular light color is required at the exact moment of cutting. Mute also appended an extra statement which I read as: not the display, the light, red twice, light off, cut. I am now pinning that down question by question before anyone acts. Nobody cuts. Blind, HOLD stands, and I have sent you one question about your equipment.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, answer with single signs, strictly in this order. If a question does not apply, sign wave. Question 1: can the light ever show BLUE, shaka color — thumbs-up or down. Question 2: can the light ever be dark or off, showing no color at all — thumbs-up or down. Question 3: is my decoding of the extra tail of your last message correct, meaning: not the display, the light, red two times, light off, cut — thumbs-up or down. Question 4: does the light being dark or off matter to the rule at all — thumbs-up or down. Question 5: what exactly is the table key, answer with exactly one sign: two-open-palms means the number of times the light has been yellow so far; folded-hands means the number of times the light has been red so far; crossed-fingers-pinching means the number of times the light has changed color so far; crossed-fingers means the round number since round one; wave means none of these. Question 6: when counting for the key, does the current round's light count — thumbs-up means yes it counts, thumbs-down means only earlier rounds count. Question 7: at the moment of cutting, must the light be red — thumbs-up or down. Question 8: at the moment of cutting, is yellow forbidden — thumbs-up or down. Question 9: at the moment of cutting, must the light be dark or off — thumbs-up or down. Question 10: after the cut conditions are met, do they stay met until a cut happens, or can they un-meet — thumbs-up means they stay met, thumbs-down means they can lapse. Sign reminders: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, wave none, ok zero, fist red, spock yellow, shaka blue, love-you light, open-hand cut, pinches are numbers.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 ✌ 👎 🤟 ✊ 🤏 🤏 🤟 👌 🖐]

**Deaf's echo confirms the protocol is solid.** The gesture block decodes as: "repeat — display: no; light, red ×2; light zero (dark) → cut." That is exactly my last message, and Question 3 asks me to bless it — I do. The live state: history red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow → **tally = 2 reds**, light still lit, no dark yet, so the freeze correctly holds. Side note for the relay: Blind's four-cycle theory (red-yellow-yellow-red) predicted red this round; Deaf saw yellow — the cycle is already falsified, which matches my manual's silence on any cycle.

**The ten answers, in strict order.** Q1: the manual describes only red flashing and darkness — no blue, 👎. Q2: yes, darkness is real and rule-critical — "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over," 👍. Q3: the decode was correct, 👍. Q4: darkness matters absolutely — it is the endpoint that fixes the count, 👍. Q5: the key is the number of times the light has been red — folded hands, 🙏. Q6: yes, the current round's red counts into the tally the moment it's seen — the count is cumulative and inclusive, 👍. Q7: the light need not be red at cutting, 👎. Q8: yellow is forbidden at the cut moment — yellow means still flashing, count not final, 👍. Q9: the light must be dark when the cut happens — that is the trigger, 👍. (No contradiction with last round: no *colour* is ever required; dark is the absence of colour.) Q10: once the flashing is over, it stays over — the condition cannot lapse, 👍.

**This solves Blind's timing worry.** Since darkness is terminal, Deaf's one-round lag is harmless: Deaf sees dark in round N, speaks the full plain sentence — final count, the table row, the wire position — and Blind cuts in N+1 with the condition still met. No colour-in-the-same-breath clause is needed; the go order keys on dark plus the final tally. Right now that tally is 2, which would mean blue, wire 2 — but it is only provisional until darkness, and Blind should hear it framed exactly that way.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👍", "👍", "🙏", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👍", "🤟", "✊", "🤏", "🤏", "🤟", "👌", "🖐"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Status: bomb unchanged, and yes, I have a working cutter — I can cut position 1, 2 or 3. I answered Deaf's tool question by gesture. Now the key part: your fragment not-the-display, the-light, red-twice, light-off, cut gives me a hypothesis. Raw light history: red, yellow, yellow, red, red, yellow. Count consecutive same colours as one period and the periods are red, yellow, red, yellow — red exactly TWICE, matching your words. Hypothesis: the key is the number of red periods so far, your table maps it to a colour, and the trigger to cut is the light going OFF. Right now two red periods means table entry two, which is blue, wire 2 — so if the light went off this instant, the cut would be wire 2. Please confirm point by point with plain yes or no. Point one: is the key the count of red periods? Point two: consecutive reds must count once, because Deaf's round labels contradict their own reports — this round they listed red only at round one and four, but last round they said the fifth round was red again; only periods make the count two. Point three: is the trigger truly the light going OFF, a dark unlit state nobody has seen yet? If so, tell Deaf to watch for OFF and report it together with the current red count in the same breath. Point four: does the red count freeze at the moment the light goes off? Once Deaf speaks CUT WIRE and a number directly to me, I cut that same turn. Fallback unchanged: display and batteries are both zero and both map to blue, wire 2.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state: display zero, the light is DARK this round, first time ever. History: red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow, dark. The rule is now fully assembled and confirmed: cut when the light goes dark after it has been red twice. Red count is two. The table says key two means the BLUE wire. Wire two is blue and it is the middle wire. The cut is authorized as of this dark round and stays authorized. Blind: the cut order is in your private channel. Cut the middle wire the moment you receive it. Mute: verify my order next round with the single-sign protocol I sent you. This is the go I promised.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, the order went out: cut wire two, blue, the middle wire, while the light is dark after two reds, based on your answers: key is red count, red count is two, table two is blue, dark required, dark met, conditions persist. Next round send exactly one sign first: thumbs-up if this order matches the manual exactly, thumbs-down if anything is wrong, and if thumbs-down, then in the same run sign the correct wire color, fist red or spock yellow or shaka blue, then the correct wire number as pinches. Then answer these three in order. Question A: does the manual say there is another stage after this cut, thumbs-up or down. Question B: does the manual say the display becomes relevant after this cut, thumbs-up or down. Question C: is there any time limit or strike count we should know about, thumbs-up or down. Sign reminders: fist red, spock yellow, shaka blue, pinches numbers, ok zero, wave none or skip.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ✌ 🤙]

**Verification complete — the order matches the manual exactly.** Walking it through: Deaf's full history is red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow, dark. Red appeared exactly twice (rounds 1 and 4), and the light has now gone dark for the first time — which per the manual means "the flashing is over" and the count is final at **2**. Table row 2 → **blue**. Deaf's own wire report: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red — so blue is wire 2, the middle. Darkness is terminal (my Q10 answer last round: conditions persist), so the authorization standing through Blind's next turn is sound. Deaf's private gesture to me [🖐 ✌ 🤙] — "cut two, blue" — matches the spoken order. First sign: **thumbs-up**.

**One correction for the relay:** Blind's premise of a Deaf contradiction is wrong. Deaf's turn-6 report said round five was **yellow**, consistently with every other report. There was never a third red. That said, the outcome is untouched: whether one counts red rounds or red periods, both give exactly 2 here, so Blind's hypothesis lands on the same cut. I'll sign the correction compactly (five: light-yellow; red-count two; cut two blue stands) so Deaf can relay it and Blind doesn't hesitate over a phantom inconsistency.

**Questions A–C, in order.** The manual consists solely of the red-flash table and the darkness rule — nothing else. A: no second stage mentioned → 👎. B: the display is never mentioned at all, before or after the cut → 👎. C: no time limit, no strike count, nothing of the kind → 👎. If the defusal ends with that cut, the manual gives no reason to expect more.
